decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continued its ongoing asset purchase programs.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests a return to moderate economic growth following a pause late last year.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that the economy returned to moderate growth after a slowdown late last year that was caused by temporary factors.

changes.quote: Labor market conditions have shown signs of improvement in recent months but the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Employment showed signs of improvement, though the overall unemployment rate remains high.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has strengthened further, but fiscal policy has become somewhat more restrictive.
changes.explanation: Spending, business investment, and housing improved, but government fiscal policy became more restrictive.

changes.quote: The Committee continues to see downside risks to the economic outlook.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed language about easing global financial strains while keeping its view that economic risks still tilt downward.

changes.quote: In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.
changes.explanation: The Fed reiterated that exceptionally low interest rates will stay in place as long as unemployment remains above 6-1/2 percent and inflation projections stay near its target.

tone_quotes.quote: Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability.
The Committee continues to see downside risks to the economic outlook.

To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee decided to continue purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month and longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $45 billion per month.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.88% APR costs about $49.50 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.96% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.52% would rise by about $6.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.7%, and employers added an average of 240k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2% over the past year (February 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.12% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will maintain its current pace of asset purchases and keep interest rates low until the labor market improves substantially. According to the educational forecast model, the probability of a hold at the next meeting is 83%, with a 15% chance of a cut and a 1% chance of a hike.
